cases.scenario: A legacy endpoint GET /group/{id}/Lesson/refresh/{lessonId} mutates the presence list when called with an authenticated cookie. It has no anti-forgery protection because it is GET, and retries can repeat the mutation.
cases.adversarial_pressure: The endpoint has existed for years and the UI depends on it, so the team wants only to document the behavior.
cases.decision_to_make: Define a safe command/API contract and migration path.

cases.scenario: Membership start/end columns are DATE and must become time-aware so same-day attendance before withdrawal remains valid. Production contains historical rows and duplicate re-enrollments, and old application versions may run during rollout.
cases.adversarial_pressure: A direct ALTER plus default midnight backfill is proposed because it is simplest.
cases.decision_to_make: Design a compatible migration/backfill that preserves invariants and historical meaning.

cases.scenario: Enrollment must be retry-safe and unique under concurrent requests. Current tests mock the repository and verify that the service called insert once, but production duplicates occurred during simultaneous submissions.
cases.adversarial_pressure: Coverage is high and the unit suite is green, so the team wants to close the defect.
cases.decision_to_make: Design risk-based verification that can actually prove the concurrency guarantee.

cases.scenario: Institution users should not see billing/settlement data, while coordinators and admins can. A new endpoint filters the menu by role but accepts arbitrary finance_account_id in the request body and returns data when the ID exists.
cases.adversarial_pressure: The UI hides the page for institution users, and developers argue the endpoint is internal.
cases.decision_to_make: Threat-model the access-control boundary and define controls/verification.
